claimed_invariant: Description-diagram actor and use-case background styles are parsed as HColorGradient values. When DriverEllipseSvg paints the first shape using a gradient, DriverRectangleSvg.applyFillColor asks SvgGraphics#createSvgGradient for a definition. SvgGraphics keys definitions by resolved color1, color2, and policy, deduplicates equal keys, assigns IDs as 'g' plus the UML-source seed plus a zero-based first-use index, emits policy-specific endpoints, and stores the definition under <defs> before the body. Actor and use-case shapes that share the same gradient therefore reference one source-seeded definition even when several entities use it.
causal_divergence: Rust already computes the Java-compatible source seed during preprocessing and already has a generative first-use gradient model for Sequence diagrams. The no-oracle UseCase renderer does not use either capability: it takes gradient definitions only from OracleLayout, passes None to gradient_fill_or, and deliberately collapses every HColorGradient to its first flat color. Cerulean therefore has otherwise-correct actor/use-case geometry and styles but lacks the three definition nodes and emits #59B6EC instead of url(#g1k3twfgxk2yb30).
planned_model_change: Add a no-oracle UseCase gradient registry driven by the actual Description paint order. Resolve each actor/use-case background to a typed color-or-gradient key, register gradients lazily in first painted-shape order, deduplicate by resolved color pair and policy, and derive IDs from the parser-carried __svgIdSeed prefix with the ordinary source-hash fallback. Serialize definitions with SvgGraphics endpoint and attribute ordering, then feed the same registry-owned URL fills to actor/use-case emission. Oracle mode continues to consume captured definitions only as a regression net. Prefer extracting the existing Sequence registry logic into a shared renderer model when that reduces duplication without changing Sequence behavior.
perturbation_axes: one shared gradient versus two distinct gradients and repeated reuse
vertical, horizontal, and diagonal gradient policies
actor first versus use-case first paint order
theme-expanded source seed versus plain source-hash fallback
renamed labels and changed entity counts
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns generative SVG gradient identity, deduplication, definition serialization, and fill references for no-oracle UseCase/Description actor and use-case backgrounds. It does not own padding, ellipse fitting, actor geometry, Graphviz layout, typography, non-gradient colors, shadows, comparator tolerance, baselines, skips, or fixture eligibility.
acceptance: The valid Cerulean UseCase golden is structurally equivalent through the no-oracle path without changing geometry or text metrics.
Fresh valid inputs prove first-use ordering, deduplication, at least two gradient policies, source-derived IDs, renamed labels, and changed entity counts.
Flat-color, transparent, and no-gradient controls retain their existing output.
An independent checker audits the Java and Rust registry data flow, generates held-outs over at least two axes, and records a verdict at the exact implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: copying gradient definitions or IDs from golden SVGs
special-casing theme names, source labels, expected SVG dimensions, or known gradient literals
using declaration order when it differs from actual shape paint order
changing comparator tolerance, baselines, skips, or fixture eligibility
evidence_inputs: fresh valid gradients with changed policies, entity order, labels, and counts
